## Summary

Related issue: #36960.

The existing `/health` endpoint remains a lightweight liveness check. It can return HTTP 200 while an alive EngineCore is unable to execute model work, for example when a GPU operation hangs or a busy engine stops making forward progress.

This PR adds `GET /ready`, which combines two complementary readiness signals:

- while the engine is busy, detect ranks that have stopped completing model steps;
- while a single-DP engine is idle, run a guarded dummy batch through the executor/GPU/model-forward path; and
- report an intentionally sleeping or paused engine as not ready without executing GPU work.

The same state is shared across API server processes and aggregated by the DP supervisor.

## Behavior

| Engine state | `/health` | `/ready` | Readiness behavior |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Dead | 503 | 503 | Reuses the existing `EngineDeadError` path |
| Busy and completing model steps | 200 | 200 | Reads cached progress; adds no probe-triggered GPU work |
| Busy without model-step progress past the configured threshold | 200 | 503 | Reports the stalled EngineCore rank(s) internally |
| Single DP, idle, and dummy batch succeeds | 200 | 200 | Exercises the executor/GPU/model-forward path |
| Single DP, idle, and dummy batch fails or times out | 200 | 503 | Does not permanently mark EngineCore dead |
| Deployment-wide DP size greater than one and idle | 200 | 200 | Skips the idle dummy batch to avoid an uncoordinated collective |
| Sleeping or paused | 200 | 503 | Returns `{"status":"not_ready","reason":"sleeping"}` |
| Render-only server | 200 | 200 | No EngineCore is attached |

`/health` semantics are unchanged. `/ready` returns a diagnostic JSON body only for the expected sleeping state; other successful or failed responses remain status-only.

## Implementation

### Explicit EngineCore readiness state

EngineCore exposes an internal `EngineCoreReadyState` with three states:

- `IDLE`
- `BUSY`
- `SLEEPING`

The state and a monotonically increasing `ready_progress_seq` are published to all connected frontend processes through `EngineCoreOutputs`. State transitions are published immediately. Continuous progress is published at most once per second to limit additional IPC traffic.

The progress sequence advances after a model step completes with scheduled tokens. DP-coordinated dummy work also records progress. Each frontend tracks the latest state, sequence, and progress timestamp for every managed EngineCore rank.

The frontend marks an EngineCore busy before sending a request. This starts the stall timer even if the core hangs before processing the request.

### Busy-engine readiness

`AsyncLLM.check_health_gpu()` first performs the existing liveness check. It then returns not ready if any managed rank:

- reports `SLEEPING`; or
- remains `BUSY` without model-step progress for longer than `VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S`.

This path only reads state already broadcast to the frontend. It does not queue a readiness RPC on an EngineCore that may already be stalled and does not add GPU work while user traffic is running.

### Idle GPU probe

For deployment-wide DP size one, `/ready` runs an EngineCore utility call only when every managed core is `IDLE`. EngineCore checks the authoritative scheduler, batch-queue, DP-wave, and sleep state again immediately before executing the dummy batch.

The idle probe has the following safeguards:

- successful probes are cached in EngineCore for a configurable TTL;
- concurrent HTTP probes share one in-flight frontend task;
- timing out an HTTP wait does not cancel or duplicate the underlying utility task;
- the dummy batch is skipped if the engine becomes busy or sleeping before the utility call executes; and
- failed probes are not added to the success cache.

### Data-parallel and multi-frontend behavior

For deployment-wide DP size greater than one, readiness still checks progress for every managed rank, but does not initiate idle dummy work. This avoids entering a MoE/DP collective on only one rank.

Readiness state is broadcast to every API server connected to an EngineCore, so the result does not depend on one frontend's local `OutputProcessor`. Tracked rank mappings are synchronized after elastic DP scale-up and scale-down.

The DP supervisor's `/ready` and `/readyz` handlers concurrently query every child `/ready` endpoint and return 503 if any child is not ready or cannot be queried. A readiness failure does not change supervisor lifecycle state or trigger shutdown by itself.

## Configuration

| Environment variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT` | 20 seconds | Frontend wait timeout for an idle GPU probe |
| `VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S` | 60 seconds | Maximum time a busy EngineCore may make no model-step progress; `0` disables stall detection |
| `VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S` | 10 seconds | Cache lifetime for a successful idle probe; `0` disables caching |

The variables are excluded from compilation-cache factors. `/ready` is excluded from Prometheus HTTP-handler instrumentation, matching `/health`.

This change does not modify Helm defaults, Kubernetes manifests, or README deployment guidance.

## Related work and non-duplication

This proposal consolidates two readiness mechanisms already being discussed:

- #46811 adds an idle dummy-batch GPU readiness probe;
- #43122 adds busy-period forward-progress detection;
- #45526 added decode-progress detection and is closed; and
- #36451 checks whether EngineCore can answer an IPC utility request.

Compared with #46811, this implementation also:

- returns not ready while sleeping instead of probing released allocations;
- avoids idle dummy execution for DP greater than one;
- checks EngineCore-global scheduler state rather than one API server's local request state;
- shares one in-flight probe and caches successful results;
- detects busy-engine stalls; and
- aggregates child readiness in the DP supervisor.

Compared with #43122, progress is based on completed model steps rather than only emitted decode tokens. It therefore covers prefill and decode, maintains state per EngineCore rank, proactively broadcasts progress, and also verifies idle GPU execution for single-DP deployments.

An IPC ping such as #36451 proves that the EngineCore process and utility path can respond, but it does not execute a model forward pass. Conversely, the idle dummy probe cannot safely cover idle DP collectives. The combined state machine makes those limitations explicit.

## Limitations

- An idle DP deployment with size greater than one does not run a GPU execution probe. Readiness can only observe state and subsequent busy progress there.
- A legitimate model step, remote-KV wait, or collective taking longer than the configured stall timeout may temporarily return 503.
- A timed-out GPU operation cannot be cancelled. Sharing the in-flight task prevents repeated probes from accumulating, but it cannot interrupt a stuck CUDA kernel.
- The endpoint currently identifies sleeping explicitly, while other failures remain status-only and require logs or metrics for diagnosis.

## Test plan and results

Tested commit: `d2e3a8a770acef195d8646095e7e0c5f9a99276e`.

Test environment:

- 2 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 GPUs with 32607 MiB each; driver 610.43.02;
- PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132 and CUDA 13.2;
- the current branch installed as a precompiled editable package, version `0.1.dev20875+gd2e3a8a77.precompiled`;
- `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, downloaded through ModelScope, for dense-model tests; and
- a locally generated 49 MiB random Mixtral MoE model for multi-port external DP. This model was used only for serving/readiness behavior, not model-quality evaluation.

```bash
uv venv --system-site-packages --python /usr/bin/python3.12
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
uv pip install -r requirements/test/cuda.in
```

The GPU fault-injection tests used shortened readiness intervals:

```bash
export VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S=5
export VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT=10
export VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S=2
```

TP=2:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 .venv/bin/python \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --dtype float16 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 512 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --port 18000
```

- Baseline `/health`, repeated `/ready`, post-generation `/ready`, and a 16-token generation all succeeded.
- The two TP workers occupied separate GPUs.
- During a 200-token request, TP1 received `SIGSTOP`. After seven seconds, `/health` returned 200 and `/ready` returned 503.
- After `SIGCONT`, readiness returned to 200 and a subsequent short generation succeeded.

PP=2:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 .venv/bin/python \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --dtype float16 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 512 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --port 18000
```

- Baseline `/health`, `/ready`, and a 16-token generation succeeded.
- Pausing PP1 produced `/health=200` and `/ready=503`.
- After resuming PP1, the original 200-token request completed and both readiness and subsequent generation recovered.

Internal DP=2 with multiple API servers:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 .venv/bin/python \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --dtype float16 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 512 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --port 18000
```

- `api_server_count` defaulted to two, with both API servers sharing port 18000.
- Six baseline readiness requests, two concurrent generations, and the post-generation readiness request all succeeded.
- With eight concurrent long requests and DP1 paused, four `/health` requests all returned 200 and ten `/ready` requests all returned 503.
- After resuming DP1, all eight requests completed, four readiness requests all returned 200, and a subsequent generation succeeded.

Multi-port external-DP supervisor:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 .venv/bin/python \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /root/vllm-ready-tiny-mixtral \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size-local 2 \
  --data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb \
  --data-parallel-supervisor-port 19256 \
  --dtype float16 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 --generation-config vllm --port 18000
```

- DP0 and DP1 listened on 18000 and 18001; the supervisor listened on 19256.
- Both child `/health` and `/ready` endpoints and the supervisor `/health`, `/ready`, and `/readyz` endpoints returned 200. Concurrent generation through both child ports succeeded.
- After pausing DP1, both child readiness endpoints returned 503, the supervisor `/ready` and `/readyz` returned 503, and supervisor `/health` remained 200.
- After recovery, both long requests completed and child/supervisor readiness returned to 200.
- Pausing the entire `APIServer_DP1` child process kept supervisor `/health` at 200, while `/ready` and `/readyz` returned 503 after 6.42 and 6.99 seconds. After resuming the child, all three endpoints returned 200 again and the supervisor and both children remained alive.
- Supervisor `/healthz` returned 404; this PR only claims `/health`, `/ready`, and `/readyz`.
- Dense Qwen3-0.6B is rejected by external-DP configuration validation, so this path requires a MoE model.

Fault injection followed this pattern. The worker PID was resolved from the process tree and `nvidia-smi` after every server launch:

```bash
curl --max-time 60 .../v1/completions &
request_pid=$!
kill -STOP <worker-pid>
sleep 7
curl .../health
curl .../ready
kill -CONT <worker-pid>
wait "$request_pid"
curl .../ready
```

### Targeted pytest

Engine-health and DP-supervisor unit tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm_health.py \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_dp_supervisor.py -q
```

Result: `40 passed, 14 warnings in 108.53s`.

HTTP instrumentator integration tests:

```bash
PATH=/root/vllm-ready-test/.venv/bin:$PATH \
PYTHONPATH=/root/vllm-ready-test \
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_basic.py -q
```

Result: `10 passed, 14 warnings in 156.43s`.

The explicit `PYTHONPATH` was specific to this remote environment. Its virtual environment used `--system-site-packages`; without the override, server subprocesses launched by the test fixture imported the globally installed vLLM 0.29.0 package instead of the editable checkout.

Whitespace check:

```bash
git diff --check HEAD^..HEAD
```

Result: exit code 0.

### Single-GPU edge cases

Sleep/wake, TTL, and idle-probe timeout tests used:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \
VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S=5 \
VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT=5 \
VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S=2 \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b --enable-sleep-mode \
  --dtype float16 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 512 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --port 18000
```

- After `POST /sleep?level=1`, `/is_sleeping=true`, `/health=200`, and `/ready=503` with `{"status":"not_ready","reason":"sleeping"}`.
- Waking only the `weights` tag left the engine sleeping and `/ready=503`. Waking `kv_cache` then produced `/is_sleeping=false`, `/ready=200`, and a successful eight-token generation.
- Probes after TTL expiry took 23.31 ms and 28.83 ms. The cache hit immediately after the first probe took 2.15 ms; all three returned 200.
- Pausing an idle EngineCore kept `/health=200`; `/ready` returned 503 after 5.002 seconds. After `SIGCONT`, readiness returned to 200 and generation succeeded.
- After repeated `/ready` requests, `/metrics` contained zero lines for `handler="/ready"`; the `/v1/models` control request had 15 related HTTP handler metric lines.

Busy-stall detection was disabled with:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S=0 \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b --dtype float16 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --port 18000
```

During a 900-token request, the EngineCore was paused for seven seconds. `/health` and `/ready` both remained 200. The request completed in 17.20 seconds after resuming and final readiness was 200, directly confirming that zero disables stall detection.

### Render-only

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main launch render \
  /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b --port 18100
```

Result: `/health=200`, `/ready=200`, and `/v1/models=200`, with no compute process reported by `nvidia-smi`.

Hi @lio1226 ,

Thanks for this PR. Having this endpoint will be very useful for vLLM server health, for online serving and RL use-cases.

I was actually working on the same feature this week and noticed this PR. My main use-case is being able to easily detect recoverable failures i.e probabilistic errors that you might hit so that a health monitor can decide to restart the server. 

Overall, I think this readiness endpoint should cover the following vLLM server failures: 

| Issue | Brief description | Failure mode |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| [\#44185](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44185) | DP \+ EP \+ MTP/speculative decoding can hang near `max_model_len` when DP ranks disagree about whether the drafter path should run. | EngineCore forward/collective hang; processes may stay alive while affected requests stop making progress. |
| [\#43547](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43547) | MoE \+ DP can drift collective sequence after zero-token scheduled steps skip DP coordination, eventually hanging a real MoE collective. | EngineCore forward collective hang, likely with worker processes alive but blocked in `reduce_scatter` or a related collective. |
| [\#36594](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/36594) / [PR \#51481](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51481) | DPEP pause/wake coordination can leave DP ranks or the coordinator in the wrong running state around `pause_generation`, `sleep()`, `collective_rpc`, or online weight update. The older issue covers a late `START_DP_WAVE` re-arming a paused engine; the later PR fixes the coordinator assuming engines started merely because it forwarded a wake. | DP wave/coordinator control-plane hang: processes can stay alive, but drain times out, frontends may stop sending `FIRST_REQ`, or ranks can enter mismatched collectives during weight-sync/control RPCs. |
| [\#53130](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53130) | Running chunked-prefill work can consume the scheduler token budget every step, so waiting/deferred requests are not admitted or promoted. | Admission starvation / request-level timeout, not a full EngineCore hang; existing running requests may still progress. |
| [\#54173](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54173) | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next prefix-caching/GDN path can hit CUBLAS internal error or illegal memory access in fused Mamba/GDN kernels. | Kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure after the async CUDA error surfaces. |
| [\#37035](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37035) | MTP/hybrid GDN illegal memory access under load, later tied to a drafter block-size/cache-pressure bug. | Kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure; may require long-running/load-heavy traffic to trigger. |
| [\#60109](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60109) | HiSparse \+ GLM TP8 on B200 hits illegal memory access when a new request wave is admitted after a previous wave completes. | Wave-transition kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure. |
| [\#59768](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59768) | SimpleCPUOffloadConnector can hit illegal memory access while async CPU-to-GPU prefix load is in flight. | Connector/load-side CUDA race causing EngineCore or worker failure, especially on prefix-cache/offload paths. |
| [\#45388](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45388) | KV-offloading plus prefix caching can deadlock the V1 scheduler under KV-cache pressure: the engine reaches `running=0`, `scheduled=0`, waiting requests remain stuck, and throughput stays at zero. | Scheduler/request-progress hang with EngineCore process alive |


Your PR covers most of the issues, however, I would suggest three changes:
1. Support cases where a busy scheduler is wedged under DP> 1: Address #45388 for MoE DP> 1. We should mark an engine as making progress with dummy batches only if there were no pending local unfinished reqs. Otherwise you could have a case where `running=0` `waiting > 0` but the scheduler still doesn't schedule any reqs. 
2. Add E2E covering basic failure modes (GPU failure, scheduler being wedged, etc): I think the readiness endpoint needs solid e2e checks since it can be extremely useful to detect failures. vLLM should have good coverage for reporting failures IMO.
3. Support for long running calls without explicit engine pause: In some scenarios there might be a `collective_rpc` being executed by the engine (ex: weight sync, some custom profiling, etc) without an explicit `/pause`. In such cases, the readiness probe will return 503 after the 20s deadline, which is fine, but I would want to return the reason for the timeout. This will enable downstream applications to decide if the engine is actually unhealthy or just doing some work. For example, even if the engine was not paused, and we triggered a long weight sync when idle, you will see this response from `/ready` after the 20s deadline:
```bash
 // Weight sync: paused, and the update is still running on the workers                                                                                                                                                
  {"status": "not_ready", "reason": "sleeping",                                                                                                                                                                         
   "message": "Engine is sleeping or paused (engine ranks: [0])",                                                                                                                                                       
   "engine_ranks": [0],                                                                                                                                                                                                 
   "in_progress": [{"operation": "collective_rpc:update_weights", "engine_rank": 0, "elapsed_s": 12.4}]} 
```

After these changes, I also did a manual test where I ran all the above failure cases as E2E tests. For #53130, I reverted the fix #51481 - the DP rank that received a generation request reports unhealthy after the stall timeout. All tests passed.

I have addressed all the three changes in a commit in my fork - built on top of your branch -  see: af7f114b32df3029161052146bd87939069aa9f4

I think this branch should add the same commit and then the PR will be ready. cc @aoshen02

Compared with #43122, progress is based on completed model steps rather than only emitted decode tokens. It therefore covers prefill and decode, maintains state per EngineCore rank, proactively broadcasts progress, and also verifies idle GPU execution for single-DP deployments.

An IPC ping such as #36451 proves that the EngineCore process and utility path can respond, but it does not execute a model forward pass. Conversely, the idle dummy probe cannot safely cover idle DP collectives. The combined state machine makes those limitations explicit.

## Limitations

- An idle DP deployment with size greater than one does not run a GPU execution probe. Readiness can only observe state and subsequent busy progress there.
- A legitimate model step, remote-KV wait, or collective taking longer than the configured stall timeout may temporarily return 503.
- A timed-out GPU operation cannot be cancelled. Sharing the in-flight task prevents repeated probes from accumulating, but it cannot interrupt a stuck CUDA kernel.
- The endpoint currently identifies sleeping explicitly, while other failures remain status-only and require logs or metrics for diagnosis.

## Test plan and results

Tested commit: `d2e3a8a770acef195d8646095e7e0c5f9a99276e`.

Test environment:

- 2 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 GPUs with 32607 MiB each; driver 610.43.02;
- PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132 and CUDA 13.2;
- the current branch installed as a precompiled editable package, version `0.1.dev20875+gd2e3a8a77.precompiled`;
- `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, downloaded through ModelScope, for dense-model tests; and
- a locally generated 49 MiB random Mixtral MoE model for multi-port external DP. This model was used only for serving/readiness behavior, not model-quality evaluation.

Environment setup:

```bash
uv venv --system-site-packages --python /usr/bin/python3.12
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
uv pip install -r requirements/test/cuda.in
```

The GPU fault-injection tests used shortened readiness intervals:

```bash
export VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S=5
export VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT=10
export VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S=2
```

### Two-GPU serving tests

TP=2:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 .venv/bin/python \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --dtype float16 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 512 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --port 18000
```

- Baseline `/health`, repeated `/ready`, post-generation `/ready`, and a 16-token generation all succeeded.
- The two TP workers occupied separate GPUs.
- During a 200-token request, TP1 received `SIGSTOP`. After seven seconds, `/health` returned 200 and `/ready` returned 503.
- After `SIGCONT`, readiness returned to 200 and a subsequent short generation succeeded.

PP=2:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 .venv/bin/python \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --dtype float16 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 512 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --port 18000
```

- Baseline `/health`, `/ready`, and a 16-token generation succeeded.
- Pausing PP1 produced `/health=200` and `/ready=503`.
- After resuming PP1, the original 200-token request completed and both readiness and subsequent generation recovered.

Internal DP=2 with multiple API servers:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 .venv/bin/python \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --dtype float16 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 512 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --port 18000
```

- `api_server_count` defaulted to two, with both API servers sharing port 18000.
- Six baseline readiness requests, two concurrent generations, and the post-generation readiness request all succeeded.
- With eight concurrent long requests and DP1 paused, four `/health` requests all returned 200 and ten `/ready` requests all returned 503.
- After resuming DP1, all eight requests completed, four readiness requests all returned 200, and a subsequent generation succeeded.

Multi-port external-DP supervisor:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 .venv/bin/python \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /root/vllm-ready-tiny-mixtral \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size-local 2 \
  --data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb \
  --data-parallel-supervisor-port 19256 \
  --dtype float16 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 --generation-config vllm --port 18000
```

- DP0 and DP1 listened on 18000 and 18001; the supervisor listened on 19256.
- Both child `/health` and `/ready` endpoints and the supervisor `/health`, `/ready`, and `/readyz` endpoints returned 200. Concurrent generation through both child ports succeeded.
- After pausing DP1, both child readiness endpoints returned 503, the supervisor `/ready` and `/readyz` returned 503, and supervisor `/health` remained 200.
- After recovery, both long requests completed and child/supervisor readiness returned to 200.
- Pausing the entire `APIServer_DP1` child process kept supervisor `/health` at 200, while `/ready` and `/readyz` returned 503 after 6.42 and 6.99 seconds. After resuming the child, all three endpoints returned 200 again and the supervisor and both children remained alive.
- Supervisor `/healthz` returned 404; this PR only claims `/health`, `/ready`, and `/readyz`.
- Dense Qwen3-0.6B is rejected by external-DP configuration validation, so this path requires a MoE model.

Fault injection followed this pattern. The worker PID was resolved from the process tree and `nvidia-smi` after every server launch:

```bash
curl --max-time 60 .../v1/completions &
request_pid=$!
kill -STOP <worker-pid>
sleep 7
curl .../health
curl .../ready
kill -CONT <worker-pid>
wait "$request_pid"
curl .../ready
```

### Targeted pytest

Engine-health and DP-supervisor unit tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm_health.py \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_dp_supervisor.py -q
```

Result: `40 passed, 14 warnings in 108.53s`.

HTTP instrumentator integration tests:

```bash
PATH=/root/vllm-ready-test/.venv/bin:$PATH \
PYTHONPATH=/root/vllm-ready-test \
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_basic.py -q
```

Result: `10 passed, 14 warnings in 156.43s`.

The explicit `PYTHONPATH` was specific to this remote environment. Its virtual environment used `--system-site-packages`; without the override, server subprocesses launched by the test fixture imported the globally installed vLLM 0.29.0 package instead of the editable checkout.

Whitespace check:

```bash
git diff --check HEAD^..HEAD
```

Result: exit code 0.

### Single-GPU edge cases

Sleep/wake, TTL, and idle-probe timeout tests used:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \
VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S=5 \
VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT=5 \
VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S=2 \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b --enable-sleep-mode \
  --dtype float16 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 512 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --port 18000
```

- After `POST /sleep?level=1`, `/is_sleeping=true`, `/health=200`, and `/ready=503` with `{"status":"not_ready","reason":"sleeping"}`.
- Waking only the `weights` tag left the engine sleeping and `/ready=503`. Waking `kv_cache` then produced `/is_sleeping=false`, `/ready=200`, and a successful eight-token generation.
- Probes after TTL expiry took 23.31 ms and 28.83 ms. The cache hit immediately after the first probe took 2.15 ms; all three returned 200.
- Pausing an idle EngineCore kept `/health=200`; `/ready` returned 503 after 5.002 seconds. After `SIGCONT`, readiness returned to 200 and generation succeeded.
- After repeated `/ready` requests, `/metrics` contained zero lines for `handler="/ready"`; the `/v1/models` control request had 15 related HTTP handler metric lines.

Busy-stall detection was disabled with:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S=0 \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b --dtype float16 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --port 18000
```

During a 900-token request, the EngineCore was paused for seven seconds. `/health` and `/ready` both remained 200. The request completed in 17.20 seconds after resuming and final readiness was 200, directly confirming that zero disables stall detection.

With the default 60-second threshold and `--max-model-len 8192`, a 7,000-token request ran for 77.24 seconds. `/ready` returned 200 at 15, 30, 45, 60, and 75 seconds while the request was still active, and after completion. This verifies that a long request with continuing model-step progress is not marked stalled merely because its total duration exceeds the default threshold.

### Render-only

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main launch render \
  /root/vllm-ready-qwen3-0.6b --port 18100
```

Result: `/health=200`, `/ready=200`, and `/v1/models=200`, with no compute process reported by `nvidia-smi`.

OpenAI Codex was used to help inspect the implementation, search related community work, analyze differences, and draft this PR description. I have manually reviewed all code changes, understood the implementation and am able to justify it, and re-run relevant checks on the final commit before submission.

Hi @lio1226 ,

Thanks for this PR. Having this endpoint will be very useful for vLLM server health, for online serving and RL use-cases.

I was actually working on the same feature this week and noticed this PR. My main use-case is being able to easily detect recoverable failures i.e probabilistic errors that you might hit so that a health monitor can decide to restart the server. 

Overall, I think this readiness endpoint should cover the following vLLM server failures: 

| Issue | Brief description | Failure mode |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| [\#44185](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44185) | DP \+ EP \+ MTP/speculative decoding can hang near `max_model_len` when DP ranks disagree about whether the drafter path should run. | EngineCore forward/collective hang; processes may stay alive while affected requests stop making progress. |
| [\#43547](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43547) | MoE \+ DP can drift collective sequence after zero-token scheduled steps skip DP coordination, eventually hanging a real MoE collective. | EngineCore forward collective hang, likely with worker processes alive but blocked in `reduce_scatter` or a related collective. |
| [\#36594](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/36594) / [PR \#51481](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51481) | DPEP pause/wake coordination can leave DP ranks or the coordinator in the wrong running state around `pause_generation`, `sleep()`, `collective_rpc`, or online weight update. The older issue covers a late `START_DP_WAVE` re-arming a paused engine; the later PR fixes the coordinator assuming engines started merely because it forwarded a wake. | DP wave/coordinator control-plane hang: processes can stay alive, but drain times out, frontends may stop sending `FIRST_REQ`, or ranks can enter mismatched collectives during weight-sync/control RPCs. |
| [\#53130](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53130) | Running chunked-prefill work can consume the scheduler token budget every step, so waiting/deferred requests are not admitted or promoted. | Admission starvation / request-level timeout, not a full EngineCore hang; existing running requests may still progress. |
| [\#54173](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54173) | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next prefix-caching/GDN path can hit CUBLAS internal error or illegal memory access in fused Mamba/GDN kernels. | Kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure after the async CUDA error surfaces. |
| [\#37035](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37035) | MTP/hybrid GDN illegal memory access under load, later tied to a drafter block-size/cache-pressure bug. | Kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure; may require long-running/load-heavy traffic to trigger. |
| [\#60109](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60109) | HiSparse \+ GLM TP8 on B200 hits illegal memory access when a new request wave is admitted after a previous wave completes. | Wave-transition kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure. |
| [\#59768](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59768) | SimpleCPUOffloadConnector can hit illegal memory access while async CPU-to-GPU prefix load is in flight. | Connector/load-side CUDA race causing EngineCore or worker failure, especially on prefix-cache/offload paths. |
| [\#45388](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45388) | KV-offloading plus prefix caching can deadlock the V1 scheduler under KV-cache pressure: the engine reaches `running=0`, `scheduled=0`, waiting requests remain stuck, and throughput stays at zero. | Scheduler/request-progress hang with EngineCore process alive |


Your PR covers most of the issues, however, I would suggest three changes:
1. Support cases where a busy scheduler is wedged under DP> 1: Address #45388 for MoE DP> 1. We should mark an engine as making progress with dummy batches only if there were no pending local unfinished reqs. Otherwise you could have a case where `running=0` `waiting > 0` but the scheduler still doesn't schedule any reqs. 
2. Add E2E covering basic failure modes (GPU failure, scheduler being wedged, etc): I think the readiness endpoint needs solid e2e checks since it can be extremely useful to detect failures. vLLM should have good coverage for reporting failures IMO.
3. Support for long running calls without explicit engine pause: In some scenarios there might be a `collective_rpc` being executed by the engine (ex: weight sync, some custom profiling, etc) without an explicit `/pause`. In such cases, the readiness probe will return 503 after the 20s deadline, which is fine, but I would want to return the reason for the timeout. This will enable downstream applications to decide if the engine is actually unhealthy or just doing some work. For example, even if the engine was not paused, and we triggered a long weight sync when idle, you will see this response from `/ready` after the 20s deadline:
```bash
 // Weight sync: paused, and the update is still running on the workers                                                                                                                                                
  {"status": "not_ready", "reason": "sleeping",                                                                                                                                                                         
   "message": "Engine is sleeping or paused (engine ranks: [0])",                                                                                                                                                       
   "engine_ranks": [0],                                                                                                                                                                                                 
   "in_progress": [{"operation": "collective_rpc:update_weights", "engine_rank": 0, "elapsed_s": 12.4}]} 
```

After these changes, I also did a manual test where I ran all the above failure cases as E2E tests. For #53130, I reverted the fix #51481 - the DP rank that received a generation request reports unhealthy after the stall timeout. All tests passed.

I have addressed all the three changes in a commit in my fork - built on top of your branch -  see: af7f114b32df3029161052146bd87939069aa9f4

I think this branch should add the same commit and then the PR will be ready. cc @aoshen02
